c4f1da693af6b0106ffedb87215e9996f229b02b.summary: CrowdStrike blog on removable-media risk, covering data theft by insiders and malicious devices entering endpoints. Its main case study is MUSTANG PANDA's USBFect USB worm campaigns (2023 to 2025), which used loaders to deliver LingerRAT, spread from the Philippines to Taiwan, and were later seen affecting organisations in North America. It also cites late 2025 USB-delivered CoinMiner campaigns and a 2025 case in which a U.S. defense engineer admitted moving over 3,600 files to personal storage. The text promotes CrowdStrike Falcon Data Protection and Falcon Device Control.

c44102b7092e8536bff0af1b062bbf436d3f3966.summary: Joint research by Flashpoint and RiskIQ, relayed by KrebsOnSecurity in November 2018, describes hundreds of fake e-commerce shops set up on expired domains to skim payment card data. The report counts more than 800 such sites since June 2018 and links them to Magecart, described as a collective of at least seven cybercrime groups. Stolen card data is sold in online cybercrime shops, and some actors sell live access to hacked stores. Two non-commercial anti-abuse organisations and Shadowserver help sinkhole hacked domains.

c43a981d5309c42ec57ba10f5e2d5b64846ef2b6.summary: Mandiant's research on the FIN7 cybercrime group. It describes merging eight suspected UNC groups into FIN7 in January 2022 and FIN7's heavy use of PowerShell tooling, including the POWERPLANT backdoor. Access methods named include phishing, supply chain compromise and stolen credentials. Possible ties to ransomware operations are described as a possibility, and Mandiant had not attributed direct ransomware deployment to FIN7. UNC3319 and UNC3381 are suspected to be FIN7 with low confidence.
